newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German unemployment hits record in November.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German unemployment hits record in November.

text.p: German unemployment climbed to another post-unification record in November, rising 50,000 to 4.1 million on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Federal Labour Office said on Thursday.
The adjusted unemployment rate was 10.7 percent, compared with 10.1 percent in October, the Bundesbank said.
The rise, while expected at the start of winter, was larger than many economists had forecast.
"It's really quite substantially more than expected," James Stewart of SE Banken in London told Reuters Financial Television.
"The basic message that we are seeing from the economy is mixed... It's really unclear in which direction the economy is headed," Stewart said.
Economic growth in the third quarter picked up to 0.8 percent from the previous quarter, but is expected to slow again in the final quarter of the year.
But even the higher growth rates are not enough to give a substantial boost to the German employment market, which is dogged by structural problems and high wage costs.
Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said, "Recovery and growth still don't have the strength to stop the unfavourable development in the labour market."
In western Germany, the number of people out of work on a seasonally adjusted basis rose 34,000 to 2.942 million, while east Germany the number of jobless rose 17,000 to to 1.176 million.

"The production data for October and now the unemployment rate for November...show that the recovery is only export driven, and will flatten out in the next quarter and next year," said Christian Sobotta of LGT in Frankfurt.

But others were more sanguine. Michael Klawitter of WestLB in Duesseldorf said, "The labour market is a lagging indicator for the economy, so I'm still convinced that the recovery is on track. I would say that overall we should not have a too pessimistic view on the German economy."
On an unadjusted basis, the number of Germans out of work rose 3.942 million in November from 3.867 million.

Stewart of SE Banken said, "It's quite possible that fourth quarter (growth) will be weaker, but as we move into next year we would expect exports to pick up as the global economy gathers momentum. There is excessive dependence on exports, but that is not unusual for the German economy."
